lesson_title: Grow the Pie or Share the Pie?
hook_text: Two babies born in South Africa on the same day can start life with a gap wider than almost anywhere on Earth.
clip_script: One goes home to a suburb, a fee-paying school and savings. One goes home to a village, a long walk to school and a child support grant. Economists measure that gap with a number called the Gini: zero means everyone equal, one means one person has everything. South Africa scores about zero point six three, one of the highest in the world. The budget fights back from both ends: more income tax from people who earn more, and grants, free schools, clinics and houses for people who have less. But here is the real question: grow the pie or share the pie? Share it and people eat today. Grow it and there are jobs tomorrow. At three percent growth the pie doubles in twenty-four years. At one percent, seventy. The best way to share a pie? A job.
visual_style: A whiteboard split screen of two cots, a Gini scale from zero to one with a marker at 0,63, then a pie that is first sliced differently and then drawn bigger.
mood: Thoughtful and urgent, ending in a hopeful punchline.
pacing: Slow opening on the two babies, a quick Gini reveal, a brisk pie comparison, a firm last line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and decide how you would grow and share the pie.
